svg.title: Where each part of the loop fails
svg.desc: Failures land on the model call, the harness, the tool, and the sandbox, and each one stops the login-form task in a different place.
svg.text: The provider returns a rate limit, an overload, or it closes the stream halfway.
A context-length error means this prompt is too long for another try of the same prompt.
The login-form task is paused inside the harness, waiting on a reply that ended early.
The sandbox has the half-written test from the previous tool, and it is idle.
The process exits, the laptop sleeps, or the thread grows past the context window.
Compaction can fail on its own, and then every new message hits the same length error.
The harness can also loop: pytest fails, the model runs pytest again, and the transcript fills
with the same log. A huge tool result can be the thing that pushes the next call over the limit.
The model names a tool the harness lacks, or the arguments are the wrong shape.
The command runs and exits with an error. A truncated log can look like success to the model.
The printed output can contain a sentence that tries to redirect the task. The harness pastes it back.
The room runs out of memory or disk during pytest. The platform reaps an idle machine.
A write is killed halfway, and the test file is left half-saved.
With the harness outside, the transcript is still there, and a fresh room can be opened.
With the harness inside, the transcript ends with the room. A copy stored elsewhere is what remains.
